item.text: I’m checking the 2024 record directly for concrete translation of Sharif’s program into appointments, budgets, timelines, and enforcement, then I’ll synthesize the strongest positive and negative claim-level items into a compact note.

item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Sharif did translate the 2024 program into concrete priorities and mechanisms, especially in macro stabilization, education, social protection, privatization, and anti-theft enforcement. The translation was real but strongly PM-centered and only partly institutionalized, with counterevidence from personalized control and coercive oversight.

**Accepted Claims**
- [PM declares education emergency to enroll 26 million out-of-school children](https://www.radio.gov.pk/08-05-2024/pm-declares-education-emergency-to-enroll-26-million-out-of-school-children) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-08 | Sharif set a numeric enrollment target, said he would personally supervise the program, and tied it to provincial coordination, girls’ incentives, and Daanish Schools. This is direct evidence of a concrete priority with an execution target. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- [Pakistan IMF reaches staff-level agreement on economic policies for 37-month EFF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | IMF | 2024-07-12 | The program explicitly linked policy to a FY25 budget that expanded BISP, education, and health spending, and to a National Fiscal Pact that shifted more social spending to provinces. It also constrained discretionary supplementary grants except in disasters. This is strong evidence of a program translated into budgets, intergovernmental arrangements, and enforcement limits. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [Pakistan: 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement under the EFF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr) | IMF | 2024-09-27 | The IMF said the new program aimed to entrench macro stability, broaden the tax base, strengthen competition, reform SOEs, improve the FDI regime, and support a fairer business environment. It also noted that weak governance, low investment, and a narrow tax base remained. This shows a structured policy package, but one still only partly implemented. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- [PM directs to minimize load-shedding](https://www.radio.gov.pk/28-05-2024/shehbaz-sharif-directs-to-minimize-load-shedding) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-28 | Sharif ordered an anti-power-theft campaign, monthly personal review, provincial and law-enforcement support, task forces at provincial and divisional levels, no overbilling, and expert hiring for DISCO privatization. This is concrete enforcement machinery, not just rhetoric. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [All state-owned enterprises to be privatised: PM](https://www.dawn.com/news/1833439/all-state-owned-enterprises-to-be-privatised-pm) | Dawn | 2024-05-15 | Sharif said all non-strategic SOEs would be privatized, ministries were told to cooperate, power distribution companies were folded into the 2024-29 privatization programme, and a pre-qualified expert panel would be appointed. This is a clear example of a priority turned into an implementation structure. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [Pakistan PM Sharif picks prominent banker in new cabinet, document shows](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-sharif-picks-prominent-banker-in-new-cabinet-document-shows/1996146/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-11 | Aurangzeb, a career banker, was brought into cabinet for the finance portfolio. That is a technocratic appointment aligned with the stabilization program, and it signals an attempt to staff the economic agenda with credibility. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [PM Shehbaz relieves finance minister from key economic forum](https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967/pm-shehbaz-relieves-finance-minister-from-key-economic-forum) | Dawn | 2024-06-15 | Sharif took personal chairmanship of ECNEC instead of leaving it to the finance minister. This shows active central control over implementation, but also weakens the case for full institutional delegation. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- [BISP digital wallets to ensure transparent, convenient payments](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/) | APP | 2024-03-18 | Sharif directed full digitalization of BISP payments to reduce leakage, delay, and discretion. That is a concrete delivery mechanism that turns a social priority into a rule-based administrative tool. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [Cabinet composition and old-guard staffing](https://www.dawn.com/news/1821157) | Dawn | 2024-03-01 | Reporting on the new cabinet said it still leaned heavily on established political figures. This weakens the idea of a clean technocratic break and suggests the program was only partially depoliticized in staffing terms. | `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`
- [Government clamps down on dissenting media, opposition, and NGOs](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | HRW said the government increased pressure on media and critics, deepening self-censorship and fear. This is negative evidence that enforcement mechanisms were also used to protect regime space rather than simply deliver the declared program transparently. | `8B.2`, `7B.10`, `7B.8`
- [X blocked on national-security grounds](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | The state acknowledged blocking X around the election period on national-security grounds. This is a concrete enforcement action, but it also shows the government using communications controls in a politically sensitive way. | `8B.2`, `7B.10`, `7B.8`
- [Pakistan government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | Critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations. That is strong counterevidence to any claim that Sharif was building neutral institutions to carry the program forward. | `8B.2`, `7B.10`, `7B.8`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a single 2024 “master plan” document or public implementation scorecard that cleanly ties all priorities together.
- The best evidence is fragmented across IMF program documents, PM speeches, cabinet decisions, and specific enforcement meetings.
- That means the answer is inferential: Sharif clearly translated parts of the program into concrete actions, but the institutional depth and consistency of execution were uneven.
